complexity_ledger.justification:
COMPLEXITY INCREASED IN THE MODULE THIS TICKET TOUCHED, and the ledger's own delta says zero because its declared model is SkillManager.tla, which is untouched. Stating the real number rather than accepting the convenient one: HomeIntegrityInternal went from 10 variables / 8 actions / 6 configurations to 28 variables / 23 actions / 18 configurations, and the healthy run from 10 distinct states to 24,000.
THE ESSENTIAL BEHAVIOUR THE ADDED REPRESENTATION CARRIES. Nine properties this epic FIXED in production and that nothing anywhere asserted: a tree identical to the live source is disposable whatever its record names (HIS-1), a divergent one is not (HIS-1), one gate is surfaced in full at most once (HIS-3), an unacknowledged gate still refuses a launch (HIS-3), a reported error is a function of the live tree (HIS-4), a clone's sanction is re-derived from the parent's own store rather than granted by its record (HIS-10), a home's two axes name one home (HIS-14), an observation never repairs what it observed (HIS-13 / DEF-067), and a damaged home is never reported clean (HIS-13). Each is carried by its own disjoint variable group, each has an expected-violation configuration that fails on IT and on nothing else, and that isolation is measured rather than asserted -- see tlc/CROSSCHECK-target-removed.txt.
WHAT THE INCREASE COSTS, stated because it is the part a later reader needs: the six groups are DISJOINT, so the healthy state count is a PRODUCT. A seventh group multiplies rather than adds, and 24,000 of budgets.max_distinct_states = 50,000 is already half the ceiling. Filed as DEF-087 together with the observation that nothing runs these configurations automatically at all.

complexity_ledger.narrative:
results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-5/goal-contribution.md is the narrative ledger. Read section 3 first -- it is the part the machine-checked core above cannot express.
THE FINDING THIS TICKET IS ACTUALLY ABOUT. TLC reports the FIRST invariant it finds violated, in an order the author does not control, so a configuration written to refute invariant X can be refuting invariant Y for years and read identically in every transcript. "The regression cfg fails" is therefore a claim about iteration order, not about the invariant. Every one of the fourteen expected-violation configurations here was consequently re-run with its TARGET REMOVED and the other thirteen invariants kept, and had to come back green. Fourteen greens. That is vacuity-ledger mechanism A answered by measurement rather than by reading a trace, and it is the check a reviewer should attack first -- transcript at tlc/CROSSCHECK-target-removed.txt.
THE SAME QUESTION FACING THE OTHER WAY. Nine invariants that HOLD is not the claim that nine were EVALUATED: every one is an implication or an equality, and an implication whose antecedent is unreachable is TRUE and worthless. This view has already nearly shipped that exact defect once -- ARTI-22's ProjectionSourceIsDecidable had "foreign" unassigned and TLC could not distinguish it from TRUE. Two reachability probes were added, following External.NoWorktreeEditEverReachesTheRootHome, and BOTH MUST FAIL; the second one's counterexample is a nine-state trace in which the antecedent of every remaining new invariant is live at once.
THREE THINGS I AM NOT CONFIDENT ABOUT, in the order a reviewer should test them. (1) NOTHING RUNS THESE CONFIGURATIONS -- run_tlc.sh has no caller in test_graph, in pytest or in CI, and the graphs are suspended on push and PR, so the manifest's expected_violations map is a table only a human re-running eighteen commands can falsify. An assertion nobody runs is the same defect as an assertion that cannot fail, one level up. DEF-087. (2) The HIS-11 omission is the weakest of the two: a write witness would make it statable, the way External.sync_history was added for exactly this reason, and I did not add one. (3) AnObservationNeverRepairsWhatItObserved is TRUE of the desired instrument and FALSE of the shipped one, because DEF-067 is open -- so specs/current now asserts something the product does not do, and specs/current and specs/desired_program_model are byte-identical for this module, which leaves the distinction nowhere to live.

refinement.detail:
FOUR smaller representations were considered. Three were taken and one is recommended and NOT applied.
TAKEN (1): three of the five extra candidate properties were argued and DROPPED rather than modelled. HIS-9's write confinement is already External.WritesThroughOneHomeReachNoOtherHome and External.NoOwnedSurfaceNamesAnotherHome (dual_representation_rule); HIS-11's compensation is already Internal.InFlightMaterializationLeavesTheChildUnitIntact; and DEF-036 / DEF-040, both routed to this ticket as "state it as an invariant", were REFUSED because a bounded model in which the author writes both derivations cannot catch two Java methods drifting apart -- an assertion that would pass forever regardless of the code, which is the defect #217 exists to prevent. Recorded as DEF-088. That is five properties' worth of variables not added.
TAKEN (2): HIS-1's two clauses were NOT collapsed into the single equality `hi_held_back <=> (hi_unit_content # hi_live_source)`, which would have been one invariant instead of two over the same variables. Rejected because each clause has an INDEPENDENT counterexample -- the record-consulting rule and the dispose-everything rule -- and the collapsed form gives them one configuration and one report line, which is exactly the shape that lets a fix that went too far read as a fix that worked.
TAKEN (3): the HIS-1 pass is ONE action rather than a present-then-decide pair, which removes an intermediate state in which a divergent tree is not yet held back and would have forced clause 2 to be weakened to "...once the pass is done" -- a guard a broken model satisfies by never finishing a pass.
RECOMMENDED, NOT APPLIED: give each of the six property groups its OWN specification over its own variable set, following this repository's existing `two_specs_per_module` precedent, instead of one HomeIntegritySpec over all 28 variables. That turns the healthy state count from a PRODUCT of the groups into a SUM. It was not applied because the single healthy specification is what lets HomeIntegrityInternal.cfg check all thirteen invariants in one run against a home that reaches all of their antecedents, which the two reachability probes then demonstrate; splitting it needs six healthy configurations and a decision about where the cross-group reachability probe lives. Advisory, unapproved, and named as the decision most likely to look wrong at the next extension.

summary: HIS-5 (#217): nine invariants over HomeIntegrityInternal, one per behavioural fix this epic made, each with an expected-violation cfg that fails on its OWN invariant (measured: 14 cross-checks with the target removed, all green); one guard cfg for the single witness-dependent invariant; two reachability probes that must fail; all five pre-existing regression cfgs still fail.

goals.expected_effect: 4 invariants / 5 cfgs -> one new invariant per fix, each with a failing cfg, all 5 originals still failing

ticket.objective: ARTI-22 gave the home-integrity view 4 invariants and 5 regression cfgs. None of them state the four properties this epic fixes, so all four can regress silently. Extend the view; do not restate anything the legacy monolith already says (dual_representation_rule).
ticket.slice: One invariant per fix, each with an expected-violation cfg that FAILS, and for each, an explicit statement of whether it is witness-dependent (guard_config_rule). Candidates, to be settled in the ticket: - an identical tree is disposable regardless of what its record names; - a divergent tree is not; - an acknowledged gate is surfaced at most once in full; - a recorded error is a function of the live tree, not of history. Re-run ALL pre-existing regression cfgs; a cfg that starts passing is a defect in the invariant, per regression_config_rule.
ticket.status_note_delivered: DELIVERED. NINE invariants, not four: the plan's four candidates were all settled and stated (HIS-1 both clauses, HIS-3 both halves, HIS-4), and four more were added after arguing each of the five candidates the plan did not list. STATED BEYOND THE PLAN, with the reason in each case. SanctionIsRederivedFromTheParentsOwnStore (HIS-10) -- a clone's descent is a POINTER, not a GRANT; the invariant mentions the descent record NOWHERE, so it refutes both faces review rejected, the hand-written home.provenance.json and the clone-time snapshot that keeps sanctioning after the parent revokes. HIS-10's own plan row promised GOAL-home-invariants a "direct" contribution and discharged it against `jbang RunTests.java`; this is the TLA+ half of that promise, arriving seven promotion slots late. AHomesTwoAxesNameOneHome (HIS-14) -- stated because NO module in this directory models the agent axis. External's homes have one axis, which is also why DEF-076 could measure a dangling projection in every ticket worktree's .codex and .gemini with nothing to notice it. AnObservationNeverRepairsWhatItObserved and ADamagedHomeIsNeverReportedClean (HIS-13 / DEF-067) -- the first is the one WITNESS-DEPENDENT invariant here and the only one that describes behaviour the product STILL HAS. DEF-067 is open. NOT STATED, deliberately. HIS-9's write confinement: the at-rest half is External.WritesThroughOneHomeReachNoOtherHome and External.NoOwnedSurfaceNamesAnotherHome, and restating it is what dual_representation_rule forbids; the refusal and its exit code are a command-surface property this view does not model. HIS-11's compensation: the rule is Internal.InFlightMaterializationLeavesTheChildUnitIntact and External.AConflictedUnitIsNeverPartiallyWritten, and HIS-11's actual defect -- an EMPTY compensation list -- is invisible to an at-rest invariant, which cannot tell "restored" from "never touched". CLAUSE 2 HELD: all five pre-existing regression cfgs still FAIL, each on its own invariant, individually re-run and individually reported. THE CHECK WORTH REVIEWING FIRST. Every expected-violation cfg carries its NEIGHBOURING invariants as well as its target, and all fourteen were additionally re-run with the TARGET REMOVED and the other thirteen kept: fourteen greens, so each counterexample violates exactly one invariant and it is the declared one. That is vacuity-ledger mechanism A answered by measurement rather than by reading the trace. Two REACHABILITY PROBES were added for the same reason facing the other way -- nine invariants that HOLD is not the claim that nine were EVALUATED -- and both must FAIL.
